don’t think I’m heavy.
What do you think?
How much do you weigh?
It was Hada’s turn to get
weighed. We never leave him
out. He seems to have grown so
much. Bada: Mom, what
about Hada? Mom: Yes. I need to know
his weight. Bada:
I’ll get him. Oh, he is
heavy, Mom. Mom: Put him
on the scale. Oh, no. He needs to
be still. I
know what. Let me hold him and we’ll get weighed
together. Hana: Then you can get
weighed alone. Mom: That’s right.
Let’s see. Come here,
Hada. We weigh 61.5
kilograms. Now Hada can sit down.
I will check my weight.
I weigh 52 kilograms. So
how much does Hada weigh? Hana:
Hada weighs 9.5 kilograms. Mom:
That is correct. Hada
weighs quite a lot.
He grows so fast.
Hear the Christmas carols.
See the twinkling lights.
It’s the Christmas season!
Hana: Mom, Christmas is just around the
corner. Mom: Yes,
dear. Bada: I can’t wait for Santa to
come. He will give me a nice present.
Dad: What do you wish to
get? Bada: Well, this year, since I have been such a good boy . .
. I wished for a nice pair of
rollerblades. Dad: Hmm. Really? I see . .
. Bada: What about you,
Hana? What did you ask for?
Hana: I asked for a mini camera.
I like to take pictures.
Dad: Boy, Santa will need to work very hard this year.
Hana: Done! Bada, quick!
Turn off the light! Bada:
Okay, here we go.
Everyone: Wow! It’s beautiful!
Santa Claus brings happiness to us all!
It was a bright Christmas morning.
Bada: Is it morning
yet? My present! Hana, get up!
It’s Christmas morning! Hana:
Huh? Oh, yes!
Bada: Where is my gift?
Here it is! Wow,
it’s heavy. Hana: Here
is mine too. Bada:
Wow, how cool! Dad, look! These
roller blades are exactly what I wanted! All right! Hana:
This camera is perfect. Thank
you, Santa! Bada: Mom,
may I try the roller blades right now? Mom:
You can go out after you eat breakfast, Bada.
Bada: Boy, I am hungry.
Mom, please fix me some breakfast quickly!
What a sweet day.
Merry Christmas, everyone!
Mom has big news.
Do you want to hear about it?
Dad: Mom has some news for you
guys. Mom: Do you remember Aunt
Sunny? Bada: Who is
that? Hana: Oh, I remember her,
Mom. She is your best
friend. She came to Korea last year.
Mom: That’s right. But call her Aunt Sunny.
She is like a sister to me.
We were invited to her wedding! Hana:
That means we are going to America? Mom:
Except for Dad. He
has to work. Hana: Sorry,
Dad. But don’t worry. I
will take lots of pictures and bring them back to you. Dad: Thank
you, dear. Bada: What
about Hada, Mom? Mom:
Grandma will take care of him. Hana:
How long are we staying? Mom:
We will stay for about a month. Yes,
a trip to America!
I will tell you all about it.
Wait and see!
I guess I am not dreaming.
I am at the
airport! Hana: Okay, Bada. Strike a pose and I will take
a picture. Bada: Sure. How
is this? Hana: Good.
Say, "Cheese!" One, two,
three! Mom: We are all set
to go. You’d better say good-bye to Dad
now. Hana: So soon?
Oh, Dad. I will miss
you. Bada: Me too. I will call you every
day, Dad. Dad: Oh, I will miss you
guys too. Call me when you
get there. Mom: We
will, honey. Please take care of
Hada. Dad: Don’t worry
about him. Hana and Bada, listen to your mom and behave
yourselves. Have a safe
trip. Hana & Bada: Bye, Dad. See you
later. We will miss you. Bada:
Mom, I miss Dad already. Mom:
We will see him soon, Bada. Who
can stop us now?
Here we go!

episodes.title: I Was Flying Above the Clouds!

subtitle.text: Can you imagine?
I was flying above the clouds!
Bada: This is
boring. I thought flying would be fun.
Mom: It’s almost dinnertime.
Here is the menu. We
can have either salmon or chicken. Choose one. Hana:
Hmm. I want chicken. Bada:
What is salmon? Hana:
It’s a kind of fish. Bada:
Yuck! I hate fish. I
will have chicken. Flight
attendant: Salmon or chicken? Mom:
Salmon, please. Hana:
Chicken, please. Bada:
Me too. Chicken, please. Flight
attendant: Anything to drink?
Mom: Yes, I will have some water.
Hana: Do you have milk?
Flight attendant: Sure, we do.
Here you go. Hana:
Thank you. Bada:
Mom, can I have a Coke? Mom:
Sorry, Bada. No Coke. Bada:
Okay. Milk, please. It
was a long flight.
But I didn’t mind.
I will have so much fun soon.
Hooray! We have finally arrived.
Mom: Let’s line up.
Bada: What now,
Mom? Mom: We show our passports to the
man. He will ask some questions. That’s all.
Immigration: Good afternoon! Your passports,
please.Where are you from? Hana:
We are from Korea! Immigration:
How long do you plan to stay? Mom:
We will stay for a month.
Hana: My Aunt Sunny is getting married!
Immigration: How wonderful!
Welcome to the United States. Enjoy
your stay here. Mom:
Thank you. Bada:
THANK YOU! Mom:
Now, we have to pick up our bags. Mom:
Hmm. Excuse me, sir.
Where is the baggage claim area? Officer:
Go straight ahead and turn right. Mom:
Thank you. Officer:
My pleasure, ma’am.
I can’t wait to go out and see the city!
Aunt Sunny and her fiancé were waiting for us. Hello,
there! Mom:
Sunny! Sunny: Oh,
Young-Hee. How have you been?
I am so glad you could come.
Hana & Bada: Hello, Aunt Sunny.
Sunny: Oh, my! Hana and Bada! Welcome,
welcome! Let me introduce you to my
fiancé. His name is Tom Blake.
Tom, this is my best friend, Young-Hee.
Tom: How do you do?
Call me Tom. Mom:
Nice to meet you, Tom.
You can call me Young. These
are my children, Hana and Bada. Tom:
Beautiful names. Hello,
Hana. Hello, Bada. Hana &
Bada: Hi. Hello. Sunny: Come
on. Let’s go home. You
guys must be tired. Tom: Here.
Let me take your bags. Mom:
Thank you. Tom:
Let’s go to the parking lot. Bada
couldn’t take his eyes off the car.
It was our first evening in San Francisco.
Sunny: This is Chinatown.
Hana: Look at the stores and the
buildings. I can hear them speak Chinese.
Bada: Oh no. I can’t speak Chinese.
Tom: Don’t worry, Bada.
They speak English too. Bada:
Whew! Tom:
Let’s go in. Waiter:
Good evening, ladies and gentleman. Sunny:
A table for five, please.
Waiter: Right this way, please.
Hana: Ni-hao-ma.
Waiter: Ho.
Tom: I didn’t know you spoke Chinese!
Hana: Just the greeting. That’s all.
Waiter: Here is the menu.
Let me know when you are ready.
Mom: Thank you.
I love Chinese food.
One day, I would like to visit China!
I couldn’t wait to eat.
I was so hungry!
Waiter: Would you like anything else?
Sunny: Just a minute, please.
Hana and Bada, do you want anything else?
Bada: I want the sweet thing with beef.
Sunny: What is that?
Hana: He means sweet and sour beef.
Sunny: Oh, I see.
Would you like that too, Hana? Hana:
I don’t mind, Aunt Sunny. I
am hungry. Sunny: Okay,
okay. A dish of sweet and sour beef, please. Waiter:
Yes, ma’am. Would you like anything to drink? Sunny:
Some cold water, please. Hana:
May I have cold water too? Waiter:
Sure. Tom:
I would like a glass of house wine, please. Waiter:
Yes, sir. Bada:
Mom, may I have a Coke, please? Mom:
Alright, Bada. Just this one time.
Bada: Yes! I would like a Coke, please.
Waiter: Right away!
Bada loves soft drinks.
They're not good for your teeth, you know!
My Aunt Sunny’s wedding is coming up.
She must be very
excited! Mom: Look! This is Union
Square. Hana: Wow, this place
is huge. Look at all the people and the
stores. Are you getting something for
Dad? Mom: No, not for
him. It’s for Aunt Sunny.
We are having a bridal shower tomorrow.
Hana: A bridal shower?
What is that? Mom:
The bridal shower is a party.
We prepare many gifts for the bride. Hana:
That’s interesting. What are you going to buy, Mom?
Mom: I’m going to buy her a
tablecloth. There. Let’s look at the store directory.
Home interior . . . Ah, here it is. H24.
Are you hungry? Bada:
No, Mom. Hana:
I’m hungry, Mom. Mom:
We’ll eat after we shop.
Is that Okay? Hana:
Sounds good. I
saw beautiful things to decorate the house with. Wow!
Yes! The store was full of beautiful things.
Clerk: Can I help you?
Mom: Yes, please. I am looking for a
tablecloth. Clerk: This way,
please. All the tablecloths are in that corner.
Let me know if you need help. Mom:
I see. Thank you.
Excuse me. Do you have this in gold? Clerk:
Oh, yes. Here you go. Mom:
That’s perfect. Thank you. Clerk:
You’re welcome. Mom:
I would like to buy these two, please.
Clerk: Sure. Cash or credit card?
Mom: Credit card, please.
Clerk: One moment, please.
Sign right here, please. Mom:
Okay. There. Clerk:
Thank you. Here is your card and the receipt.
Mom: Thanks.
What a wonderful tablecloth!
It has gold lace all around it.
After shopping, we were very hungry, so we went to eat lunch.
Mom: Hana, you can order whatever you want.
Here is the money. Hana:
What about Bada?
Mom: I will order for both of us.
Hana: Let me try.
Clerk: May I help you?
Hana: Yes. I would like a cheeseburger and a small order of French fries, please.
Clerk: Anything to drink?
Hana: A small orange juice, please.
Clerk: For here or to go?
Hana: For
here. Clerk: That’ll be $4.25,
please. Hana: Here you
are. Clerk: A five dollar
bill. That’s 75 cents change. Thank you.
Hana: Umm . . . Can I have more ketchup?
Clerk: Here you are.
Hana: And where can I get a straw?
Clerk: The straws are on the counter to your
left. Hana: Oh, I see them. Thank
you. Clerk: You are very
welcome. Next, please.
Yes, I ordered all by myself!
I did a good job!
Tomorrow, I’m going to a garage sale.
Do you know what a garage sale is?
Why don’t you come with me?
Hana: What are we doing tomorrow?
Sunny: We’re going to a garage sale.
Bada: What’s that?
Mom: Let’s find out.
Sunny: At garage sales, people sell things they don’t need or want
anymore. Mom: How much is
this? Woman: Oh, that’s fifty
cents. Hana: What’s
that? Woman: That’s a record player.
Listen. Hana & Bada: Wow! What are
these? Woman: These are cookie
cutters. You can make cookies in these shapes.
Hana: How much are they?
Woman: Ten cents each.
Bada: I like this!
Woman: It used to be my son’s.
You can have it for free! Bada:
Thank you very much! Woman
: You’re welcome!
Bada: Look what she gave me!
Hana: Look what I got!
Mom: Oh, you can make cookies now.
In America, people don’t just throw away things.
Other people may want them.
Instead, they have garage sales.
Garage sales are lots of fun!
I love reading books!
Tom: This is our public library.
Hana: So many books!
Tom: Do you like to read?
Hana & Bada:
Yes! Tom: What kind of books do
you like? Hana: I like
fairy tales. Bada: I like
COMIC BOOKS! Librarian: SHH! Please
be quiet! Bada:
Oh, sorry! Tom: We have to be quiet in
the library. Bada: Can I . . . ? Oops! Can I
read here? Hana: Can I look around
by myself? Tom: Sure, but come back
here, okay? Hana: Okay! I
love fairy tales. And I
love mysteries. Oh, and I really love animal
stories. I am interested in science too.
Tom, how many books can I borrow? Tom:
Only five books, Hana. After
you finish them, we can come back. Hana: Oh!
Thank you! Librarian: Do
you have a library card? Tom:
Yes, here you go. Librarian:
You must return these books by next week. Hana
& Bada: Bye!
I can’t wait to go back to the library next week.
Aunt Sunny and Tom are very busy.
So we’re going to see a movie.
Mom: What movie do you want to see?
Hana: The Unicorn Princess.
Mom: How about The Adventures of Max the Wonder Dog
? Hana & Bada:
Okay! Mom: One adult and two children,
please. Hana: We’re going to see The Adventures of Max the Wonder
Dog. Clerk: Okay. Enjoy the
show! Mom: Thank
you. Do you want some popcorn?
Hana & Bada: Yes!
Bada: Can I have some juice
too? Hana: Nothing for me,
thanks. Mommy, where do we sit?
Mom: You can sit wherever you like.
Bada: Really?
Mom: See? There are no seat numbers.
Hana: Bada, can you pass me the popcorn?
Mommy! Bada won’t give me the popcorn. Mom:
Bada! Voice-over
: Meet Max! The wonder dog!
Bada: The movie’s starting, Hana!
Hana: I know! Give me the popcorn!
It was a great movie!
Have you seen any good movies lately?
Going to the park is lots of fun.
There is so much to do!
Hana: Can I help you?
Mom: Can you take the paper cups over there?
Hana: Are we going on a picnic?
Sunny: Yes, we’re going to Golden Gate
Park. Tom: What do you want to do
first? Bada: Can we
rollerblade? Sunny: Sure! Let’s go rent some
skates! Hana: Watch
this! Bada: Mom! Can you take a picture of us,
please? Mom: Okay, everyone, say,
"Cheese!" Hana, Bada, Tom & Sunny:
CHEESE! Tom: Let’s go for a boat
ride. Bada: I can see
fish! Mom: Hold still,
Hana. I’m going to take a picture.
Hana: Oh, the bird flew away!
Mom: What’s over there?
Tom: That’s Queen Wilhelmina’s Garden and Windmill.
Mom: It’s
beautiful. Hana: Look at the tulips,
Mom! Sunny: Excuse me, can you take a picture of us,
please? Man: No
problem! Okay, everybody, say, "Cheese!"
Everyone: CHEESE!
We took many photographs at the park.
Do you want to see my favorite one?

episodes.title: A Postcard for Dad and Hada

subtitle.text: I miss Dad and Hada.
I wonder how they’re doing?
Sunny: Do you need anything, Hana?
Hana: Yes, I’d like to buy some postcards for Daddy and
Hada. Sunny: What a good
idea! Let’s look in this shop.
Hana: Here is a nice one.
It shows the Golden Gate Bridge. Sunny:
That’s beautiful! Hana:
I’ll take these.
Hana: Dear Daddy and Hada , How are
you? I miss you very much.
We are having lots of fun in America. Mom:
Do you want some cookies, Hana? Tom:
Hey, Hana! What did you do today?
Hana: I wrote a postcard to my daddy and Hada.
Can you take me to the post office? Tom:
Sure thing. Let’s go. Clerk:
Hello. What can I do for you today? Hana:
I want to send this postcard to Korea.
Clerk: Korea? Okay, that’ll be 75 cents.
Hana: Here you go.
Mom: Did you send the postcard, Hana?
Hana: Yes. I hope Daddy likes it.
When will he get it? Tom:
Probably in a week or so.
Since Dad can’t come to San Francisco, I sent San Francisco to him!
Aunt Sunny asked me to be her flower girl.
I get to wear a pretty dress and hold a basket full of roses.
Sunny: Today we’re going to the dressmaker’s.
Mom: You will get your flower girl dress,
Hana. Sunny: What’s your favorite
color? Hana: I like
pink. Seamstress: Now it’s your
turn. Mom: You’re going to love your
dress. Hana: Oh, it’s my favorite
color! Seamstress: Try it
on! Mom: Are you ready,
Hana? Seamstress: Oh, you look like an
angel! Mom: Hana, you look so
beautiful! Seamstress: Don’t forget the flowers in your
hair. What’s your favorite flower, Hana?
Hana: My favorite flower is the rose.
Mom: Then your basket will be filled with red
roses. Sunny: Okay, I’m ready to come
out! What do you think?
Mom: You are the most beautiful bride ever!
Hana: Aunt Sunny, you look so pretty!
Boy, now I’m hungry! Sunny:
What’s your favorite food, Hana? Hana:
I love barbecued chicken, spaghetti, and, of course, chocolate ice cream! Mom:
Hana, I think you’ve had too much to eat. Hana:
But I’m still hungry, Mommy. Sunny:
Let her enjoy her ice cream, Young-hee.
Mom: I just hope you don’t get sick!
Aunt Sunny looked so beautiful in her wedding dress.
My dress is very pretty too.
I can’t wait for the wedding day!
Ooh! I think Mom was right.
I ate too much!
Mom: What’s wrong, Hana?
Hana: I’m not feeling well, Mommy.
Mom: Where do you feel sick?
Hana: My stomach
hurts. Mom: I thought you ate too much
yesterday. Hana: I know, Mommy. I’m
sorry. Sunny: There you are,
Young-hee. Bada isn’t feeling well.
Mom: Neither is Hana.
Sunny: How are you feeling?
Hana: I have a stomachache.
How is Bada? Sunny:
He has a runny nose and a cough. Hana:
Poor Bada! I hope he’s better soon. Sunny:
I’d better go to the drugstore.
l’ll get some medicine for you and Bada. Hana:
Thank you. Mom:
My poor baby. Sunny:
Here, take this. Ahh . . . Hana:
Yuck! It tastes awful! Sunny:
You have to take this three times a day. Hana:
I wish I wasn’t sick. Sunny:
Hey, Bada! How are you feeling? Bada:
I’m hungry!
Sunny: How about some chocolate ice cream?
Hana: Not for me!
Bada and I are feeling much better now.
I’ll never eat so much ice cream again!
Aunt Sunny’s family is coming for the wedding.
We got to meet them.
Sunny: Mom! Dad! It’s so good to see you!
Mother: Sunny! How are
you? You look beautiful!
Father: You look wonderful, dear!
Sunny: Let me introduce you to my best friend, Young-Hee.
Mom: Hello. It’s nice to meet you.
Father: And what’s your name?
Hana: My name is Hana.
Nice to meet you. Bada:
And I’m Bada. Sunny:
This is my sister, Sherry. Sherry:
I’ve heard so much about you.
Mother: Where are you from?
Hana: We’re from Korea.
How many brothers and sisters does Aunt Sunny have? Mom:
She has one sister and one brother. Hana:
Where is her brother? Mom:
He is living in France. Father:
How old are you, Bada? Hana:
He’s seven years old.
And I’m ten. Mother:
So, Hana, I heard you are going to be the flower girl. Hana:
Yes. I have a beautiful pink dress. Bada:
I want to be a flower girl too! Father:
You can’t! It’s for girls only! Sherry:
The big day is coming up, Sunny. Sunny:
I know! It’s so exciting.
Hana: I can’t wait for your wedding, Aunt Sunny.
Mom: It’s going to be a beautiful wedding.
Aunt Sunny’s family is so nice!
It’s finally the big day!
Today, Aunt Sunny and Tom are getting married!
Sunny: Oh, where are my hairpins?
Mom: I’ll look for them,
Sunny. Sunny: And my
bouquet! Where is it?
Mother: It’s right here, dear.
Guest: Congratulations, Tom.
Tom: Thank you.
Where are the rings? Father:
They’re in your pocket. Relax, Tom. Mom:
Are you nervous?
Sunny: I’m very nervous.
Hana: You look beautiful.
Sunny: Thank you for everything.
Father: It’s time.
Mom: Are you ready, Hana?
Hana: Yes, but I’m nervous too.
Mom: Don’t worry. You look beautiful, Hana!
Sherry: Oh, Hana looks like an
angel! Mother: She’s so
pretty! Guest 1: Look at the
bride! She’s so beautiful! Guest
2: What a beautiful bride! Tom:
. . . I do. Minister:
And do you, Sunny, take Tom as your loving husband?
Sunny: I do.
Minister: I now pronounce you husband and wife.
Bada: Congratulations, Aunt Sunny!
Congratulations, Uncle Tom! Tom:
Thank you, Bada! Mom:
What a beautiful wedding! Hana:
Thank you for inviting us!
I am happy for Aunt Sunny and Uncle Tom.
They are going to Hawaii for their honeymoon.
While Aunt Sunny and Uncle Tom were on their honeymoon, we decided to clean the house for them.
Hana: What are you doing,
Mommy? Mom: I want to wash these for
Sunny. Hana: How are you going to wash them
all? Mom: I’m taking them to the
Laundromat. Do you want to come along?
Hana: This is my first time at a Laundromat.
Mom: Well, we need to find an empty washing
machine. Hana: Here,
Mommy! Mom: Can you change these into
coins? Hana: Can you change these into coins,
please? Woman: Here you
go. Hana: Thank
you. Mom: We’ll wash the blankets
first. Hana: They’re so
heavy! Mom: Yes, they
are. Now, push the door and turn the
dial. Then we sit here and wait!
Hana: What’s that?
Mom: That means the washing is finished.
Help me put it into the dryer, Hana. Hana:
Now, what do we do? Mom:
Do you want some soda? Hana:
What is Bada doing?
Mom: He is helping Sunny’s parents clean the house.
Hana: They feel so soft and dry!
Mom: Thanks for helping me, Hana.
Mother: We finished cleaning the house.
Bada: I helped too, Mommy!
Mom: I’m so proud of you, Bada.
And you too, Hana. Mother:
Your children are such hard workers!
Aunt Sunny’s house looks so clean!
I can’t wait for her and Uncle Tom to come home!
Guess what! We’re going to Disneyland!
But first, we have to buy a few
things. Mom: Kids, would you like to go to
Disneyland? Hana & Bada: Disneyland!
Yeah! Yeah! Mom: But first, we have to get
some things. Bada: When are we going
to Disneyland, Mom? Mom: We leave
early tomorrow morning. Hana: How are
we getting
there? Mom: We’re driving. We
need some sugar. Where
is it? Bada: Is this
it, Mom? Mom: No,
Bada. That’s flour. Hana: I’ll
go and ask. Excuse me, where is
the sugar? Clerk:
Sugar? Follow me. Here
you go. Hana: Thank you. Oh! Where
is everybody? Cereals and
pasta? No, I don’t see
them. Drinks and snacks?
Oh, where can they be? Mom?
Bada? I think I’m lost. Clerk:
What’s your name? Hana:
Hana. Clerk:
Paging Hana’s mother! Please
come to the checkout counter. Hana
is waiting for you. Mom: Hana!
Hana! Clerk: I’m
glad you found your mom, Hana. Hana:
I was scared that I lost you! Mom:
Hana, don’t worry. You’ll
never lose me! Whew!
That was a close call. I
thought I would never see my mom again! I’m
glad that clerk was so nice to help me.
We left early for Disneyland.
It was a long drive!
Bada: How long will it take,
Mom? Mom: Oh, about six
hours. Hana: Six hours? That’s a long
time! Mom: California is a very big
state. Bada: I’m
bored! Mom: Let’s play
a game! Do you know I
Spy? Hana & Bada:
Yes. Mom: Let me
start. Umm . . . I spy with my little eye something that begins with
C. Hana: Is it
carpet? Bada: Is it
coffee? Mom: Yes! Bada, it’s your
turn. Bada: I spy with my little eye, something that begins with . . . umm . .
. A. Hana: Are we
lost, Mom? Mom: I hope
not, Hana. Bada: Mom! A
man is coming. Man: Can
I help you? Mom: We’re
driving to Disneyland. Which way do
we go? Man: Turn right
at the light. Then get on
the highway. Keep going straight and you will reach
Anaheim. Mom: Thank you very
much! Look, kids! We’re in
Anaheim! We’re almost at Disneyland now.
Bada: Look at that car, Mom!
Hana: Maybe he’s a movie star!
We’re here! We’re at Disneyland! Oh,
I can’t wait to go on the rides! Bada:
Will I meet Mickey Mouse? Mom:
Of course! And Goofy and Donald Duck too! The
drive was very long, but it was worth it.
Disneyland is like a dream!
There is so much to see and do at Disneyland.
Have you been to Disneyland?
Mom: Which ride do you want to go on first?
Hana: The roller coaster!
Bada: No, I want to go on the balloon ride!
Mom: We can do both!
Bada: We’re up so high!
Hana: I feel like I’m flying.
Mom: Sit down, Hana!
Bada: They look like ants.
Mom: What do you want to ride next?
Hana: Can we ride the bumper cars?
Bada: But I want to see Mickey Mouse!
Mom: I’m sure we’ll see him soon,
Bada. Bada: Bam! I got you,
Mommy! Hana: Bam! Look out,
Bada! I’m following you!
Mom: Oh . . . Hana! Here I come!
Hana: Mommy! Let’s get Bada!
Mom: Let’s have some cotton candy.
Bada: Yummy! This tastes good.
Hana: Oh, it’s so hot!
Mom: I know a great way to cool down!
Hana: Look at the fireworks!
Bada: My ears hurt.
Hana: The show’s about to begin.
Mom: Look, Bada! It’s Mickey Mouse!
Disneyland is not only fun for children, but it’s also fun for adults.
I want to go again!
We were so tired from the wedding, so we went to the zoo to get some fresh
air. Mom: Now, stay close and listen to
me. Hana & Bada: Okay,
Mommy. Bada: Let’s see the
tigers! Mom: Come back here,
kids! Bada: Look at
the tigers! They’re so
big! Mom: Don’t lean against the
cage! Hana: Come here,
kitty. Mom: Don’t put your hand in the
cage! Hana: Look at
the elephants! Mom: Don’t feed
the animals! Hana:
Oh, sorry. Bada: Do you want some peanuts
instead, Mommy? Look at the
monkeys! They’re so
funny! Hana: I want to touch
them! Mom: Don’t touch the
monkeys! Oh, my hat!
Give that back to me! Don’t
you want to eat anything? Hana:
Whenever we do something, you always say "DON’T." Bada:
Yeah, so we don’t want to do anything. Mom:
I’m sorry. From now on, I’ll say "DO." Did
you have a good time? Hana
& Bada: Yes, Mommy. Mom:
I’m sorry I was so mean. Hana:
We love you! Mommy
was so tired, but she still took us to the zoo.
We had a good time with her.
Aunt Sunny and Uncle Tom are back from their honeymoon.
They took us on a cable car ride across San Francisco.
We had so much fun!
Hana: Can we ride a cable car?
Sunny: Yes, here comes one now!
Mom: How much is the
fare? Tom: Don’t worry. It’s on
us. Hana: Wow! San Francisco is so
beautiful! Sunny: Yes, it
is. Look! That’s City Hall.
Bada: Where? I can’t see.
Tom: Be careful, Bada.
Hang on tight! Sunny:
This is our stop. Tom:
This place is called Fisherman’s Wharf. Hana:
What is that sound? Sunny:
That must be the sea lions. Hana:
Look! Look at all those sea lions! Mom:
Oh my! There must be at least a hundred of them. Bada:
Wow! I never saw a sea lion before!
Tom: We have to get back on the cable car again.
Hana: What’s that man doing?
Tom: He is turning the cable car around so that it can go in the opposite direction.
Sunny: He’s called a gripman.
Gripman: Does anyone want to help me?
Hana & Bada: Me! Me!
Gripman: Okay, now, Push! Push!
Thanks for your help! All aboard! Mom:
Did you have a good time today? Hana:
Yes. It was a lot of fun.
Mom: I’m glad. And what about you, Bada?
Sunny: Looks like someone is ready for bed.
Bada was so excited to ride the cable car and see many other things.
He was very happy but also very tired.
So am I.
Wow! Time sure does fly!
This is our last day in the U.S.A.
Sunny: I wish you could stay longer, Young-hee.
Mom: Me too, but my husband and Hada need
me. Bada: Can I stay here,
Mom? Sunny: Yes, you can live with
us! Hana: My suitcase won’t close,
Mom! Mom: I think you have too many things,
Hana. Hana: That’s from the
zoo. That’s from Tom!
Tom: Did you enjoy your trip to the U.S.A.?
Hana: We had a great
time! Tom: How about you,
Bada? Bada: I’m going to live with Aunt Sunny and Uncle
Tom. Tom: It was so nice to meet
you. Come back and visit soon.
Hana: I hope you can come to visit Korea.
Tom: I hope so.
Time flies by so quickly. Mom:
It feels like we just came yesterday.
Bada: Why do we have to go so soon?
Mom: Don’t you miss Daddy and Hada?
Sunny: I’m going to miss you!
Mom: Come and visit us in Korea.
Tom: We will.
Sunny: Oh, Young-hee, thank you for everything.
Hana: Good-bye, Aunt Sunny.
Good-bye, Uncle Tom! Bada:
Good-bye! Sunny
& Tom: Good-bye! Take care!
It was hard to say good-bye to Aunt Sunny and Uncle Tom.
But we were looking forward to seeing Daddy and Hada.
Dad and Hada were at the airport to pick us up.
It was wonderful to see them.
Dad: Hana! Bada! Over here!
Hana & Bada: Daddy!
Dad: Welcome
home! Mom: It’s good to be
home. Bada: We’re
home! Hana: Oh, how I missed
you! Mom: Take your suitcases into your rooms,
kids. Dad: I’ll help
you. What was your favorite part of the trip?
Bada: Going to Disneyland!
Hana: I liked the cable car ride.
Mom: For me, it was the wedding.
Dad: Did you like San
Francisco? Bada: Yes! I want to go
back! Hana: But we missed you and
Hada! Dad: Next time we can all go
together. Thank you, Hana. I love it!
Mom: This is for Hada.
Hana: I loved going to San Francisco.
But this is my home sweet home! Bada:
I can’t sleep, Hana.
Hana: Me neither.
Mom: We must all have jet lag.
Hana: Jet lag? What’s that?
Mom: Right now it is afternoon in San Francisco.
So our bodies still think we're in the U.S. Bada:
Will we have jet lag forever? Mom:
No. In a few days everything will be back to normal. Hana:
I’m glad we’re back home, Mom.
I have many wonderful memories of San Francisco.
Where can I go next time?
Do you have any places you’d like to visit?
That's my brother Bada.
He is sad today.
He misses our grandmother's dog,
King. Bada: Mommy, I want Grandma to come over to our
house. Can I call
her? Mom: Okay, but let me
dial. Bada: Hello? Grandma, it’s
me. Grandma: Hi, Sweetie, how
are you? Bada: I’m fine. Grandma, can I talk
to King?
Grandma: Sure. Bada: King! Hey King!
I miss you. King, when are you coming to
see me? I hope to see you next
week, okay? Grandma: King looks
very happy. What were you two talking
about? Bada: I want King to visit me
next week. Grandma: Sure, we’ll visit you
next week. Mom: Bada, what
are you doing? Bada: I’m waiting for
Grandma and King. Mom: They won’t be
here until lunchtime. Why don’t you help
me make lunch? Bada:
Okay. They’re here! Hello, Grandma!
Hello, King. I have a present
for you. Look, this toy puppy looks just like
you. Grandma: I think King’s
scared. Bada: See, King, it’s just
a toy. King, sit! Good
boy! Here’s a treat for
you. King, down! Very good, King.
Let’s try one more. King,
roll over! What a
smart boy, King! Grandma:
Well, it’s time to go. Bada:
Oh, don’t go. Can’t
you stay a little longer? Grandma:
No, I have an important appointment tomorrow. I
have to leave now. Bada: Okay.
Bye, Grandma. Bye, King. Mom:
It was nice seeing Grandma and King. Bada:
Yes, I miss King already. My
brother Bada loves animals.
He loves King best.

episodes.title: A Special Day for Mother and Father

subtitle.text: In May, we have Parents' Day.
On this day, we thank our mother and father for everything they do for
us. Bada and I are planning a
surprise. Hana: May 8 is Parents' Day,
Bada. Bada: What's
that? Hana: It’s a special day for Mom and
Dad. Let's give them a big
surprise! Bada: What are you
doing? Hana: I'm making a card for Mom and
Dad. Bada: Can I make one
too? Hana: Of course. Here you
go. Bada: Why did you buy
the flowers? Hana: On Parents' Day we give Mom and Dad
red carnations.
Bada: Why? Hana: Red carnations mean that we love them
very much.Bada, on Parents' Day we are going to surprise Mom and Dad.
Okay? Bada:
Okay. Hana: So don't say
anything. It's a
secret. Dad: Hey, guys! What are you doing
here? Hana: Oh, hi,
Dad! Dad: Come on, let's
go home. Bada: It's a
nice day. Let's walk,
Hana. We'll see you at home, Dad!
Dad: Okay. See you!
Hana and Bada are acting strangely. Mom:
It seems they are hiding a secret.
Dad: What kind of secret?
Mom: I don't know.
Hana: I think we should cook Mom and Dad dinner tomorrow night.
Bada: But I don't know how to cook.
Hana: Let's see . . . What do they
like? Bada: They like peanut butter and jelly
sandwiches. Hana: Oh, Bada, that's what you
like. Let's make spaghetti!
Bada: Mom! Can you help
me? Mom: Later, Bada. I have to cook dinner
now. Bada: Help me,
please. Hana: Now, I need to make the
pasta. Where does Mom keep the saucepan?
Dad: Hi, Hana. Where's your
Mom? What are you doing?
Hana: Dad! You're not supposed to be here!
You'll find out soon. Please! Dad:
Okay, okay. Mom:
Can I open my eyes now? Hana
& Bada: Yes. Happy Parents' Day!
Dad: What a nice surprise!
Bada: Thank you, Mom and Dad.
We love you! Bada
and I were so happy to surprise Mom and Dad. We
are so grateful to have them as our parents.
What will you do for your parents on that special day?
Do you like flowers?
What is your favorite flower?
I like tulips.
We went to the flower festival last week.
It was beautiful!
Bada: Can we go on the
merry-go-round? Mom: Not today,
Bada. Today, we are going to see the flowers.
Hana: Come on, Bada!
Let's go look at the tulips! Bada:
But I want to go on the merry-go-round. Hana:
Oh, take a picture of me in front of the tulips, please.
Mom: Where is Bada? Bada? Bada?
Dad: Did you know there are over 30,000 flowers here?
Mom: Honey, let's find Bada first.
Dad: Oh, right. Sorry.
Bada! Bada! He can't be too far away. Bada! Bada! Hana:
Wait! I think I know where he is.
Mom: Bada! Bad boy!
You made us worry. Bada:
I’m sorry. But I wanted to see the merry-go-round. Hana:
Bada, we can go on the rides later. Bada:
Promise? Hana:
Promise. Now let's go see more flowers. Bada:
I’m sorry, Mom and Dad!
After that, even Bada enjoyed the flowers.
Of course we went back to the park to ride the merry-go-round.
So everyone was happy.
Summer vacation is just around the corner!
This year we are going to the
beach! Mom: Are we ready to
go? Do we have everything?
Dad: Yes, I think so.
Okay, everyone! Hop in! Bada:
Can I have ice cream at the beach?
Mom: Of course you can, Bada.
Hana: I want to take a boat ride.
Dad: We can do that
too. It's going to be so much fun at the beach.
Hana: Oh! And I want to build a sand castle!
Bada: Me too,
Hana! Hana: Oh, Mom! It's so
beautiful! Can we go swimming now? Please? Please?
Mom: No, it's too late.
But tomorrow we can go early in the morning. Okay?
Hana & Bada: YEAH!
Bada: Wake up! Hana! Mom! Dad!
Hana: What time is it?
Why is it so dark?
Oh no! It's raining! Bada:
We can't go to the beach! Dad:
Don't worry. We'll think of something. Mom:
Come on, you two. It's fun!
Hana: No, thanks.
Dad: Look, Bada! It's your favorite!
Chocolate ice cream! Bada:
No, thank you. I
want to eat it on the beach. Mom:
I have a great idea. Do
you still want to go to the beach? Hana: Yes,
but it's raining, Mom. We'll
get all wet! Mom:
But if you went swimming, you'll still get wet. Right? Hana:
There's no one on the beach, Mom.
Mom: That's what makes it special.
We have the beach all to ourselves. Bada:
Can we go in the water? Dad:
Of course!
Hana: This is so much fun!
Swimming in the rain is better than swimming in the sun! Oh,
look! A rainbow! It’s beautiful! It
rained again the next day. But
we still went to the beach. Dad
said we should always look on the brighter side of things.
Even if it rained, we still had lots of fun.

episodes.title: A Visit from Sunny and Tom

subtitle.text: Guess what? Aunt Sunny and Uncle Tom are coming to
visit! Aunt Sunny says she has something very special to tell
us! I wonder what it
is. Hana: When are Aunt Sunny and Uncle
Tom coming? Mom: Next Saturday. They're going to stay
with us. Bada: Where
will they sleep? Mom:
In Hana's room. So you have to sleep with your
brothers, okay? Hana: But Mom
. . . Dad: Hana. Aunt Sunny and Uncle Tom
are our guests. We want them to
feel welcome, right? Hana: Yes, Dad
. . . Sunny:
Hana, you've grown! We've missed
you so much. Hana: Me, too! I really enjoyed our trip to
California last year. Tom: Next time you come,
you'll meet someone new. Hana: New? What
are you talking about?
A new friend? Sunny: We'll
tell you later. Bada: Hana!
Read me this story! Hana: No, Bada!
I'm going to sleep. Go
to your own bed. Bada:
But I'm not sleepy! Just
this story, please? Hana: I wish I was sleeping
in my own bed. Oh, Bada
is so loud! I
can't sleep! Oh, no! There's somebody in
the kitchen! Maybe it's a
burglar. Should I wake Mom and Dad up?
What about Bada and Hada?
What if the burglar goes in there? Sunny:
Who's there? Hana? Hana:
Aunt Sunny! What are you doing here?
Sunny: Did I wake you? Sorry, Hana.
I was so hungry. Hana:
Oh, maybe you didn't have enough for dinner.
Sunny: I had a lot for dinner.
But I’m hungry again. Hana:
Oh, should I wake Mom up?
She can make you pancakes. Sunny:
No, that's okay. I
like sandwiches. Remember—Uncle Tom
said next time you visit, you'll meet someone new. Hana: Yes.
Who is it? Do I
know her? Sunny: It
may be a girl or a boy. I don't
know. Hana: You don't
know who it is? Sunny: Not
yet. Hana, I'm going to have a baby. Hana: A
baby? Sunny: Tom
and I want a family of our own. We
want children just like you, Bada, and Hada. Hana: Wow!
A baby. Aunt
Sunny is going to have a baby! I
can't wait! She
wants children just like us.
She says we're special.
I think so, too.

episodes.title: Chuseok, A Day to Give Thanks

subtitle.text: This month we have Chuseok.
It's a time to give thanks and remember our
ancestors. Mom: Hana! Grandma bought you a
gift. Hana: For me? But it's not
my birthday. Mom: I know. It's
for Chuseok. Bada: What about
me, Mommy? Where's my
present? Mom: Here you
are. Hana: Oh, Mommy! It's
so pretty! Mom: It's
lovely, Hana! You can wear that when we go to Grandma's house
at Chuesok. Hana, can you help me carry this,
please? Hana: But what if it gets on
my dress? Mom: Don't be
silly, Hana! Here, put this
on. Then your dress won't get dirty.
Hana: It's dirty,
Mom! My dress will get dirty too!
Mom: Hana! Chuseok is a day to give thanks.
It's a day we help each other and show that we love each other.
Now put this apron on! Bada:
Oops!
Hana: Oh, my dress! My dress!
Look what you did, Bada! Mom:
It's okay. We'll find something else for you to wear.
Grandma: Here comes Hana.
Come sit next to me, dear. Chuseok
is a special day to give thanks. It
doesn't matter how we look or what we eat, as long as we are together as a family. Grandma
is right. Sometimes
we forget to be thankful. I
learned a valuable lesson. It's
not important what we have but what we give.
I love autumn!
I love the blue skies.
This year we are going to Mt. Sorak to see the colorful leaves on the
trees! Dad: What are you
doing? We're leaving soon.
Bada: I don't want to go.
Hana: Can Bada and I stay
here? We don't want to go hiking.
Mom: No, you can't.
Besides, I know you'll love Mount Sorak. Now,
come on! Hana: Wow!
Look at the beautiful colors! Why
do leaves change colors? Dad: Because
the trees are getting ready for winter. Mom: All
leaves have green, yellow, and orange in them. But
in the summer, the green color is the strongest. Bada: Why?
Mom: Because
of the sun, and water from the tree. But when
the weather gets cooler, the tree gets less sun and water. Dad: So
the green fades, and the other colors like yellow and orange become brighter. Bada: Here's
a red one! Mom:
Yes! There are red and purple leaves too. Dad:
Hana, you like maple syrup on your pancakes, right? Hana:
Yummy! I love maple syrup. Mom:
Well, that syrup comes from the trees!
Hana: Wow! I never knew that!
Dad: Bada! Pick that up!
Mom: Never throw your garbage on the ground.
Bada: But
why? Dad: Do you throw garbage in your
room? In your house?
Bada: No, only in the trash can.
Mom: Well, this is the trees' house.
And it is home to the birds, squirrels, and other living things too.
We mustn't make it dirty. Do
you understand? Bada: Yes,
Mommy. Sorry, little squirrel! Dad:
Now, let's all take a picture. Hana
& Bada: CHEESE! We
spent three days in Mount Sorak. Mommy
and Daddy taught us so much. We
learned about trees, birds, and animals.
I’m glad we didn't stay inside and watch TV.
Last night my grandma got very sick.
Mommy and Daddy had to go to the
hospital. So I had to stay with Bada at
night. Hana: Is Grandma going to
be okay? Mom: I hope
so, Hana. Will you be okay looking
after Bada? Hana: Yes, don't
worry, Mom. We'll be
fine. Dad: If anything happens, call me on my cell
phone. Okay? Mom: We'll be
back soon. Dad: Don't open the door
for anyone! Hana &
Bada: We won't! Bada: Hana!
Someone is here! Hana: Mommy and Daddy said not
to open the door. From outside the door: Hana!
Bada! It’s Minji's
mom. Hana: Minji's mom? Bada:
Maybe it's not Minji's mom! Minji's
mom: Hana! Open the door! It’s
cold out here! Hana: It doesn't
sound like Minji's mom. Minji's mom: Hana! Bada! Open
this door right now! Your
mom called me! She wanted me to come
over. Now, open up! Hana:
Do you believe her?
Bada: Let's call Dad!
Hana: Oh! He's not answering. Oh, no!
Bada: Hana. Let's call the police!
Hana: Hello? Is this the
police? My name is Hana.
There is someone outside my house.
And my mommy and daddy aren't home. Police:
Hana? This is the police. Please
open the door. Hana:
Oh! It really was you! Mom:
What happened! What's going on here! Is
everything okay? Minji's
mom: Hana wouldn't open the door. I
told her it was me! Hana: But Daddy
said not to open the door for anyone. Dad: You
did the right thing, Hana. It's my
fault. Hana: I’m
really sorry. Minji's mom:
No, you did the right thing. Mom: I
should have called you, Hana, and said Minji's mom was coming. I’m
sorry. Bada: How
is Grandma? Dad:
She's going to be okay. What
a night! I'm
glad everything turned out fine. My
dad said it's always better to be safe than sorry.
It's already the end of the year!
Christmas is just around the corner.
I still haven't bought gifts for my family!
What should I give them?
Hana: I'll get this for Mommy. There!
Hana: I'm finished with my Christmas shopping.
Bada: Can I get this?
Hana: Bada! Did you get gifts for Mommy and Daddy?
Hana: What about Hada?
Bada: What kind of gifts?
Hana: Gifts that show you love them.
Hana: It's Christmas time, you know!
Hana: You have to give everyone gifts!
Bada: Hana, can you help me?
Hana: Not now, Bada. I'm busy!
Hana: I have to wrap these Christmas gifts!
Bada: Okay. Hana, can you help me?
Hana: Bada! I'm very busy right now!
Hana: I have to write these Christmas cards!
Bada: Okay.
Mom: Is Bada still sleeping?
Dad: I heard him get up.
Dad: Bada! Bada! Breakfast time!
Hana: Bada is so selfish!
Hana: He only thinks about himself.
Mom: Hana! That's not nice.
Mom: He's still young.
Mom: Give him time to learn.
Hana: I bet he doesn't have any Christmas gifts to give us.
Hana: He only likes getting them.
Dad: Hana! Why are you being so mean?
Dad: Christmas isn't about giving gifts.
Dad: It's about giving love and being with your family.
Dad: That's the best gift of all.
Mom: Good morning! What's that in the bag?
Bada: Christmas gifts!
Hana: It's not even Christmas yet!
Mom: It doesn't matter.
Mom: Bada is giving us something from the heart.
Bada: This is for you, Mommy!
Mom: Why, thank you, Bada!
Bada: And this is for you, Daddy!
Dad: Thank you, son.
Bada: And this is for Hada!
Mom: That's lovely, Bada.
Bada: And for you, Hana. Here.
Hana: "To Hana, the best sister.
Hana: I love you. Love, Bada." Oh, Bada!
Bada: Why are you crying?
Hana: Because I've been so mean to you.
Hana: I'm sorry! I promise to be a better sister.
Bada helped me see what the best gift of all is.
Like Dad said, it's about love and being with your family.
I learned a good lesson.
From now on, I'm going to try to give the best gift of all to my family, every day!
